Continue a criteria pipeline on top of an existing flow

Source: R/continue.R
continue_criteria.Rd

Applies additional criteria steps to the surviving cohort of an existing cf_flow, optionally joining on new columns first. This lets an attrition pipeline be built up in stages – e.g. apply screening criteria, then join newly collected follow-up data and continue with further criteria – while keeping a single, continuous step numbering and denominators that correctly reflect the cohort at each stage (rather than restarting counts from the original data).

Usage

continue_criteria(flow, criteria, join = NULL, by = NULL)

Arguments

flow

A cf_flow object produced by apply_criteria() (or a previous call to continue_criteria()).

criteria

A cf_criteria object with the additional steps to apply. If empty (length(criteria) == 0), flow is returned unchanged.

join

Optional data frame of new columns to attach before evaluating criteria, e.g. follow-up data collected after the initial screening. Joined onto all of flow's original rows (via a left join), so rows already excluded at an earlier stage also gain the new columns (as NA where join has no match) – this keeps the full row history intact. Requires by.

by

Column name(s) shared by flow's data and join, used to join them. Required, and only used, when join is supplied.

Value

A cf_flow object whose criteria and steps are the concatenation of flow's existing pipeline and criteria, with step numbers continuing on from flow.

Details

Before any new step is evaluated, check_criteria() verifies that every step refers only to columns present in flow's data plus join, so a forgotten join fails up front naming the step and the missing column(s).

See also

Other pipeline: apply_criteria(), cf_expected(), cf_hierarchy()

Examples

dat  <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 200, seed = 1)
crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Passed screening")
flow <- apply_criteria(dat, crit)
#> No `id` supplied and no `.cf_row_id` column found. Adding a sequential `.cf_row_id`.

more_crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consent recorded")
flow2 <- continue_criteria(flow, more_crit)
flow2
#> Cohort flow  (2 steps | 200 -> 157 rows | 43 excluded)
#> ------------------------------------------------------------
#>    1. [+] Passed screening
#>        n_in: 200  kept: 183  removed: 17
#>    2. [+] Consent recorded
#>        n_in: 183  kept: 157  removed: 26
